description: Framework-agnostic architectural layer boundary and separation-of-concerns rules for multi-tier and MVC applications.

rules.name: Zero Presentation & Frontend Code in Domain, Models & Controllers
rules.description: Strictly prohibits embedding raw presentation markup (HTML tags, JSX, CSS styles, client-side script tags, DOM manipulations) inside Domain, Model, Service, or Controller classes.
rules.rationale: Enforces strict Separation of Concerns (SoC). Models manage domain state and persistence; Controllers orchestrate application flow; Presentation belongs exclusively to dedicated Views, Templates, or Client-side components.
rules.remediation: Move presentation markup into dedicated View templates (e.g. Razor, Blade, Jinja, JSX/TSX components) or return structured DTOs / ViewModels.

rules.name: Zero Direct Database Queries in Presentation & Views
rules.description: Prohibits executing raw database queries, direct ORM invocations, or data-access commands inside presentation templates and views.
rules.rationale: Presentation templates must not handle data retrieval or query logic. Direct querying in templates causes severe performance degradation (N+1 queries) and architectural coupling.
rules.remediation: Fetch data within the Controller, Use Case, or Application Service and inject prepared ViewModels/DTOs into the presentation layer.

rules.name: Zero Transport Protocol Coupling in Domain Models
rules.description: Prohibits binding HTTP request objects, superglobals, headers, or web transport context inside Domain Entities and Models.
rules.rationale: Domain models must remain transport-agnostic to enable safe execution across CLI tools, background workers, asynchronous queues, and unit tests without HTTP mocking.
rules.remediation: Pass primitive types, Value Objects, or domain DTOs to Model methods instead of HTTP Request objects.

rules.name: Thin Controllers (Delegation to Application / Domain Services)
rules.description: Controllers and HTTP handlers must act strictly as thin entry-point coordinators and must not contain heavy domain calculations or complex algorithmic workflows.
rules.rationale: Fat Controllers hinder unit testability, duplicate business logic across entry points, and violate the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP).
rules.remediation: Extract business logic into Use Cases, Application Services, or Domain Services.

rules.name: Explicit Input Validation & Boundary DTOs
rules.description: Mutation endpoints must validate input payloads using strongly-typed Request DTOs, Validators, or Schemas before delegating to application services.
rules.rationale: Prevents malformed data from polluting domain handlers and centralizes validation and authorization rules.
rules.remediation: Declare explicit validation schemas (e.g. FluentValidation, FormRequest, Zod, Pydantic, Bean Validation) on endpoint inputs.
